audit_findings.title: Finance-lease-funded capex may escape both OE reinvestment and the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2025 finance-lease additions $136 million, principal payments $142 million, and liabilities $365 million; additions and payments equal 17.1% and 17.8% of the $795.9 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Finance-lease asset amortization may be added back in OE while the corresponding non-cash capital acquisition and financing principal payments are omitted; the $365 million liability is also outside the stated $3.378 billion notes-and-borrowings figure.
audit_findings.evidence: Certain equipment and buildings held under finance leases are classified as property, plant and equipment and the related obligation is recorded as accrued expenses and other liabilities on the Consolidated Balance Sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a recurring, economically significant finance-lease funding channel and confirms that the liabilities sit in accrued expenses and other liabilities rather than reported notes payable. Whether the OE calculation already captures the associated reinvestment is unresolved, but an omission near 17% of anchor OE is reasonably capable of materially overstating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct each OE year with finance-lease additions, asset amortization, interest, and principal payments; identify the maintenance portion and rerun all scenarios after subtracting that recurring reinvestment or otherwise consistently recognizing the liability.

audit_findings.title: The bridge appears to treat gross cash as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.360 billion added to equity value, equal to $12.56 per diluted share and 10.8% of the $12.542 billion base equity value; latest inventory deposits were $1.385 billion and contract liabilities were $992 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash and short-term investments as a non-operating asset even though some cash may be customer-funded or required to operate the working-capital-intensive business.
audit_findings.evidence: At times, we collect deposits from our customers related to the purchase of inventory in order to effectively manage our working capital.
audit_findings.explanation: The gross addition is demonstrated, but the amount that is genuinely surplus is unresolved. The customer-funding and liquidity balances are large relative to cash, although they cannot be traced dollar-for-dollar from the supplied record. Because removing even a substantial portion of the cash addition could change stated value by several percentage points, the issue is material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile cash by legal entity and jurisdiction to restricted balances, customer deposits, contract liabilities, near-term obligations, and minimum operating liquidity; rerun the bridge using only demonstrably distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: The valuation perimeter omits a completed post-year-end acquisition
audit_findings.magnitude: $133 million final cash consideration in the latest 10-Q, equal to 1.1% of the $12.542 billion base equity value; operating-value effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The May 2026 bridge incorporates Rebound's acquired assets, liabilities, and cash outlay, while the FY2025 OE anchor excludes all post-acquisition earnings and reinvestment.
audit_findings.evidence: On September 1, 2025, the Company completed the acquisition of Rebound Technologies Group Holdings Limited (“Rebound Technologies”) for cash consideration transferred of $ 134 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. Rebound's purchase price is modest relative to base equity value, but no standalone revenue, OE, maintenance-capex, or working-capital contribution is supplied. The record therefore cannot establish either the magnitude or direction of the net valuation effect, especially if acquired operations have negative near-term OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Rebound's post-acquisition operating results and purchase-accounting cash-flow details, calculate normalized equity-level OE and maintenance reinvestment, and rerun with Rebound consistently included; alternatively reverse its balance-sheet effects and value it separately.

audit_findings.title: Repeated restructuring cash costs must not be normalized away
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2023-FY2025 charges were $57 million, $296 million, and $181 million; FY2025 cash-cost categories totaled $128 million, equal to 16.1% of the $795.9 million OE anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding restructuring charges back to earnings without a recurring replacement allowance increases anchor OE and every discounted growth and terminal-value calculation.
audit_findings.evidence: We have and may be required to take additional charges in the future to align our operations and cost structures with global economic conditions, market demands, cost competitiveness, and our geographic footprint as it relates to our customers' production requirements or following divestitures.
audit_findings.explanation: The repeated charges and their predominantly cash nature are demonstrated, but the supplied record does not show whether the $795.9 million anchor added them back. If the FY2025 cash-cost portion was normalized away, the amount is large enough relative to anchor OE to materially overstate value. This is an unresolved calculation question, not a demonstrated anchor error.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the full FY2025 OE reconciliation for restructuring, severance, lease-termination, and related adjustments; if any cash costs were added back, establish a recurring allowance from filed multi-year cash costs and rerun every scenario.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified BYD indemnity remains senior to common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Any probable indemnity payment attributable to the sold Mobility Business is a non-operating claim that reduces the equity bridge without producing future OE.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, the Company agreed to indemnify BYDE from certain liabilities that may arise post-close that relate to periods prior to the Closing Date.
audit_findings.explanation: The surviving contractual indemnity is demonstrated, but the filing cannot reasonably estimate its amount or timing and reports no claim or accrual. The record therefore cannot establish materiality; nevertheless, an expected liability omitted from the bridge would overstate common-equity value.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent filings and the sale agreement for asserted claims, caps, escrows, survival periods, insurance, and accruals; estimate and deduct the probability-weighted exposure if it is no longer remote.

audit_findings.title: Gross foreign cash may carry an omitted repatriation tax claim
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $100 million unrecognized deferred tax liability, equal to $0.92 per diluted share, 7.4% of the $1.360 billion cash addition, and 0.8% of the $12.542 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Tax triggered by distributing indefinitely reinvested foreign earnings would reduce the distributable cash included in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The estimated amount of the unrecognized deferred tax liability on these reinvested earnings was approximately $ 0.1 billion.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing identifies approximately $100 million of potential tax associated with $1.2 billion of indefinitely reinvested earnings, while also stating that most foreign cash can be repatriated without tax. Even deducting the full disclosed amount would reduce base value by only about 0.8%, from $115.85 to approximately $114.93 per share, and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $310.57 market price.
audit_findings.action: Map cash by jurisdiction and deduct any specifically attributable repatriation tax in the final bridge; no full valuation rerun is needed unless later filings disclose an exposure materially above $100 million.
